accueil.titre: Help Batack open its health centre
accueil.intro: The health centre building is there. Before it can welcome its first patients, it still needs a solid roof, electrical wiring and medical equipment. Each donation funds one of these steps, and you then see what it was used for.
accueil.projetsIntro: The village committee decides the order of the work. The amounts shown are examples until the COVIDEBA provides the real figures.
accueil.impactIntro: Examples of what a donation pays for.

etapes.texte: You send your donation directly to the COVIDEBA bank or Mobile Money account, then submit the deposit receipt on this site.
The COVIDEBA chooses the next expense with a decision-support tool that always keeps a safety reserve.
Every significant expense is published here, with its invoice or a photo of the work.

aproposTexte: The COVIDEBA is the development committee of the village of Batack. It leads the village projects: drinking water, schools, health.
Since 2024, engineering students from Belgium and Cameroon have been working with the COVIDEBA. The first two phases installed a solar microgrid and built the health centre building.
accueil.appelTexte: You can donate without creating an account.
accueil.besoinTexte: First step of the works: protect the building before installing electricity and medical equipment.
accueil.parallaxeTitre: A partnership launched by the COVIDEBA
accueil.parallaxeTexte: In 2024, Prof. Chengoué Mbouyap Anatole, chair of the COVIDEBA, and his friend Prof. Pierre Dehombreux brought the committee into a partnership with engineering students from Belgium and Cameroon. A solar charging station, then power for the health centre: each project answers a request from the village.

dispensaire.titre: Complete and equip the health centre
dispensaire.description: Today, the people of Batack have to travel more than 20 km to reach the nearest health centre. Every consultation, even for everyday care, means making this long journey. The health centre building has already been built in the village, but it cannot welcome patients yet. To open it, the roof must be finished, the electrical wiring installed, and then the laboratory and X-ray equipment bought.

batteries.titre: Solar power for the health centre
batteries.description: In January 2026, a team of students from Mons and Yaoundé equipped the health centre with solar panels and batteries. They power the refrigerator that stores vaccines and the lighting for night-time care. Batteries wear out: this project funds their regular maintenance, then their replacement, so that the health centre does not depend on an unreliable power grid.
batteries.accroche: Ensure the health centre's energy self-sufficiency

ecole.description: Batack has schools, but their classrooms are dark and cramped. The COVIDEBA also has to pay teachers every month. This project funds a teacher's salary, so that primary school children have classes all year round.
ecole.accroche: Guarantee basic education for primary school children

eau.description: The COVIDEBA has already built a first drinking water network. This project extends it to the areas that are still far from it, so that more families have drinking water near their homes. The route and the cost will be set with the COVIDEBA.
eau.accroche: Make drinking water accessible to all

marche.accroche: Give the village a proper marketplace
marche.description: The market square of Batack is under construction and cannot be used yet. This project funds its fitting out, so that the village's producers and traders have a suitable place to sell. The remaining works and their cost will be set with the COVIDEBA.

route.accroche: Make Batack's road easier to travel
route.description: The road in Batack is currently a dirt track. This project funds its improvement, to make it easier for residents to get around and for goods and equipment to be transported. The route, the works and the cost will be set with the COVIDEBA.

histoire.intro: The Batack Village Development Committee (COVIDEBA) brings together residents and members of the Batack community. It leads the village's projects, such as its first drinking water network, and decides how the funds are used.

etapes.texte: The Faculty of Engineering of Mons started working with four Cameroonian universities, in Yaoundé and Douala, on engineering education. These exchanges brought to light the needs of villages far from cities, including Batack.

On the initiative of Prof. Chengoué Mbouyap Anatole, chair of the COVIDEBA, and Prof. Pierre Dehombreux, the COVIDEBA launched microprojects supported by ARES with students from the Faculty of Engineering of Mons (UMONS) and ENSPY.
First achievement: a public solar charging station for phones and lamps, in a village without a reliable power grid. A year later, the next team checked that it was still working.

From 24 to 30 January 2026, the team installed a stand-alone solar system at the health centre: a refrigerator to store vaccines and lighting for night-time care. The work was done with local technicians and the COVIDEBA, so that the village can maintain the installation.

The health centre is built but not yet in service, and the nearest hospital is 20 km away. The current phase, funded by UMONS, creates this donation site for the COVIDEBA, prepares the technical file for the health centre and looks for lasting funding, in Europe and in Cameroon. A mission to the village is planned for January 2027.

histoire.aujourdhuiIntro: Batack is a village in the Bamileke region, in the highlands of West Cameroon. Its inhabitants, who call themselves the "little people of Batack", have already carried out several projects.

lieux.texte: A primary school with a computer room, then a nursery school built with the support of Italian cooperation.
Dark and cramped: a need identified during the January 2026 assessment.
Under construction during the January 2026 mission.
Pig farming is one of the village's activities.
The building exists. It still needs to be made operational.

histoire.equipesTexte: Since 2024, the COVIDEBA has been working with students from the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Mons (computer science and management, mechanics, energy) and from the National Advanced School of Engineering of Yaoundé (industrial engineering, mechanics, computer science).

histoire.encadrement: Supervision: Prof. Pierre Dehombreux (UMONS), Prof. Fokam Bopda Christian (ENSPY) and Prof. Chengoué Mbouyap Anatole (chair of the COVIDEBA, professor at ENSPY).

transparence.intro: You should be able to check what happens to every euro. This page brings together the amounts received, the expenses and the way the committee decides.
transparence.miseAJour: Example figures. They will be calculated automatically from the register.
transparence.repartitionIntro: Your donation is split into three parts. The percentages below are examples: the real figures will be published after the first year.
transparence.methode: Method: bank fees are those charged on deposits and transfers to Cameroon. Other costs include website hosting and local management.
transparence.registreIntro: Every significant expense is published with its invoice or a photo, and with the minutes of the COVIDEBA meeting that approved it. An entry is never deleted: a mistake is corrected by a new entry, which is also visible.
transparence.registreVide: The first expenses will appear here once the management area is up and running.
decisionPoints: Priorities are set by the COVIDEBA, together with the village health workers.
A calculation tool suggests the order of expenses while respecting the order of the works: the roof comes before the medical equipment.
A safety reserve, set by the chieftaincy, always stays in the fund.
The final decision belongs to the committee: the tool suggests, the committee decides.
transparence.rapportsTexte: An annual report, with the accounts, will be published here as a PDF.

texte: Batack Village Development Committee (COVIDEBA), Batack, West Cameroon.
Site designed for the COVIDEBA by students from the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Mons and the National Advanced School of Engineering of Yaoundé.
Photos from the student missions in Batack, published with the consent of the people photographed.
The COVIDEBA, publisher of the site (see the legal notice).
When you donate: your last name, first name (optional), email address or phone number, and your deposit receipt.
The submitted receipt is stored privately and used only to verify your deposit.
To process your donation, send you a receipt and, if you asked for it, allow the approved institution that receives donations to send you a tax certificate.
The site uses a single cookie, "langue", which remembers your chosen language for one year. There are no advertising cookies and no tracking tools.
You can ask to access, correct or delete your data by writing to the address given in the legal notice.
You can also file a complaint with the Data Protection Authority (Belgium).
This site presents the projects of the village of Batack and lets you support them with a donation.
If you made a mistake in the amount, contact us: the donation can be refunded as long as it has not been transferred to the COVIDEBA.
The certificate is issued by the approved institution that receives donations, under its own conditions and the law in force.
During the preview, the amounts and projects shown are examples.
These terms may change. The date of the last update is shown at the top of the page.
